title: The Hidden Deal Killer You’re Probably Ignoring

 The Hidden Deal Killer You’re Probably Ignoring
Hi Sara,
Want to know one of the top reasons business sales die at the last minute?
The landlord.
No one thinks about them until they’re the only thing standing between you and closing—and by then, you have zero leverage.
This week, I saw a deal collapse days before closing because of a lease issue. The buyers were relocating, everything was lined up… and then they realized they had to personally guarantee the lease. Just like that, the deal was dead.
Why Landlords Hold All the Cards
If your business is in a prime location, the landlord knows they can fill that space instantly. So why should they rush to approve a new tenant?
They don’t need to play ball, and if you wait too long to negotiate, they’ll have all the power.
How to Avoid This Mess

Get the landlord involved early. Yes, confidentiality matters, but waiting until the end gives them every reason to say no.

Know that personal guarantees are standard. If you’re hoping to avoid one, be prepared to prepay rent or put up extra security.

If you’re a seller, don’t assume the lease transfer will be easy. Buyers might be excited to take over your business, but if the landlord refuses to assign the lease, the deal is dead.

Lessons from the Trenches
I’ve seen deals where landlords have:
Refused to assign a lease because they liked the current tenant and didn’t want to risk a change.

Rejected SBA-required lease terms, which make the bank the first priority if the business defaults. Landlords hate this.

Changed their mind at the last second, leaving the buyer stranded.

If you’re in a transaction right now, consider this your warning shot—figure out the lease situation before you’re deep into due diligence.

To deals that actually close,
Sara Sharp
Partner, SK&S Law Group
Business Consultant & Founder of Deal Academy
